verdict.rationale: Google's approved API design guide (AIP-185) requires every API to carry a major version in the protobuf package and REST URI path. The Cloud terms commit to at least 12 months' notice before discontinuing a service or making backwards-incompatible changes to a customer-facing API, and a dedicated deprecation-policy page lists the covered services. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the policy is honored in practice, and coverage of pre-GA versions/features, which the policy explicitly excludes.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: All Google API interfaces must provide a major version number, which is encoded at the end of the protobuf package, and included as the first part of the URI path for REST APIs

Google will notify Customer at least 12 months before: (i) discontinuing any Service (or associated material functionality) unless Google replaces such discontinued Service or functionality with a materially similar Service or functionality; or (ii) significantly modifying a Customer-facing Google API in a backwards-incompatible manner.
Any versions, features, or functionality of the Services that are pre-general availability are excluded from the Deprecation Policy.
